## Outline

- Goodness of fit: $R^2$ and adjusted $R^2$
- Testing linear constraints on $\beta$: the Fisher test
- Verification of the model hypotheses: residuals, homoscedasticity, correlation, normality
- Outliers, leverage and influential points


# Goodness of Fit (R²)

::: {style="display:none"}

$\newcommand{\and}{\quad \mathrm{and} \quad}$

$\newcommand{\P}{\mathbb P}$

> ⬅ **Previous:** [Inference](inference.qmd)  ·  **Next:** [Selection](selection.qmd) ➡

## Pythagorean Decomposition

. . .

Let $\mathbf{1}$ be the constant column vector in $\mathbb R^{n\times 1}$.

. . .

If [$\mathbf{1} \in [X]$]{style="background-color: yellow;"} (eg if we consider an [intercept]{style="background-color: yellow;"})
$$ \underbrace{\|Y-\overline Y \1\|^2}_{SST} = \underbrace{\|Y-\widehat Y\|^2}_{SSR}+\underbrace{\|\widehat Y-\overline Y \1\|^2}_{SSE}$$

In the general case,

. . .

$$\|Y\|^2 = \|Y-\widehat Y\|^2 + \|\widehat Y\|^2$$

[Good model]{style="background-color: yellow;"} if sum of squares of residuals [$SSR \ll SST$ ]{style="background-color: yellow;"}


## R²

. . .

::: {.columns}
::: {.column}
::: {.callout-note}
## R² if 1 ∈ [X]
$$R^2 = \frac{SSE}{SST} = 1-\frac{SSR}{SST}$$
:::
:::
::: {.column}
::: {.callout-note}
## R² if 1 ∉ [X]

$$R^2 = \frac{\|\widehat Y\|^2}{\|Y\|^2} = 1 - \frac{SSR}{\|Y\|^2}$$
:::
::: 

:::

- $0 \leq R^2 \leq 1$. "Better model" if $R^2$ close to $1$
- Two definitions of $R^2$ when $\1 \in [X]$ or not
- In simple linear regression $(Y_i = \beta_1+\beta_2X_i+\varepsilon_i)$: $R^2 = \hat \rho^2$ is the [square empirical correlation]{style="background-color: yellow;"} between $Y$ and $X$ ([proof](../notes/r2_correlation.qmd): $R^2$ is a squared cosine)

## Adjusted R²

. . .

Main flaw of $R^2$: [adding a new variable increases $R^2$]{style="background-color: yellow;"} (because $[X]$ is a bigger projection space)

. . .

::: {.columns}
::: {.column}
::: {.callout-note}
## Rₐ² if 1 ∈ [X]
$$R^2_a = 1-\frac{n-1}{n-p}\frac{SSR}{SST}$$
:::
:::
::: {.column}
::: {.callout-note}
## Rₐ² if 1 ∉ [X]

$$R^2_a = 1 - \frac{n}{n-p}\frac{SSR}{\|Y\|^2}$$
:::
::: 

:::

## Adjusted R²: when does it increase?

. . .

With a [new variable]{style="background-color: yellow;"}, $SSR$ decreases but [$p \to p+1$]{style="background-color: yellow;"}

. . .

[$R_a^2$​ only increases]{style="background-color: yellow;"} when adding a new variable [if that variable reduces $SSR$ enough]{style="background-color: yellow;"}.


## R² always rises, R²ₐ does not {.smaller}

. . .

```{=html}
  <div class="lm-row">true degree d <input id="raD" type="range" autocomplete="off" min="2" max="16" step="1" value="10" style="vertical-align:middle;width:130px"> <b id="raDv">10</b> &nbsp;·&nbsp; noise σ <input id="raNz" type="range" autocomplete="off" min="0.1" max="1" step="0.05" value="0.5" style="vertical-align:middle;width:90px"> <b id="raNzv">0.50</b> &nbsp; <button class="lm-btn" id="raCritBtn">+ Cₚ · AIC · BIC</button> <button class="lm-btn" id="raNew">↻ resample</button></div>

</div>
<script>
(function () {
  var cv = document.getElementById('raCanvas'); if (!cv || cv.dataset.init) return; cv.dataset.init = 1;
  var c = cv.getContext('2d'), W = cv.width, H = cv.height, N = 80, KM = 24, KEY = 'lmAdjR2';
  var dEl = document.getElementById('raD'), kEl = document.getElementById('raK'), sEl = document.getElementById('raNz');
  var xs = [], Z = [], Q = [], mu = [], Y = [], dd = [], r2 = [], r2a = [];
  var cp = [], aic = [], bic = [], kmin = {}, showC = false;
  function gauss() { var u = 0, v = 0; while (!u) u = Math.random(); while (!v) v = Math.random(); return Math.sqrt(-2 * Math.log(u)) * Math.cos(2 * Math.PI * v); }
  // Orthonormal polynomials on the design points, by the three-term recurrence
  // q_{j+1} ∝ (x - a_j) q_j - b_j q_{j-1}. Never form the Vandermonde: 1, x, ..., x^24
  // is hopelessly ill-conditioned, this recurrence is not.
  function basis() {
    var i, j, v, s, a, bp = 0;
    Q = [[]]; for (i = 0; i < N; i++) Q[0].push(1 / Math.sqrt(N));
    for (j = 0; j < KM; j++) {
      a = 0; for (i = 0; i < N; i++) a += xs[i] * Q[j][i] * Q[j][i];
      v = []; s = 0;
      for (i = 0; i < N; i++) { var t = (xs[i] - a) * Q[j][i] - (j ? bp * Q[j - 1][i] : 0); v.push(t); s += t * t; }
      s = Math.sqrt(s); bp = s;
      for (i = 0; i < N; i++) v[i] /= s;
      Q.push(v);
    }
  }
  function regen() { xs = []; Z = []; for (var i = 0; i < N; i++) { xs.push(-1 + 2 * i / (N - 1)); Z.push(gauss()); } basis(); }
  // true mean = degree-d projection of a cosine, rescaled to variance 1, so that
  // the signal-to-noise ratio stays the same whatever d (only the shape changes).
  function signal(d) {
    var g = [], m = [], i, j, b, s = 0, mn = 0;
    for (i = 0; i < N; i++) { g.push(Math.cos(d * xs[i] + 0.8)); m.push(0); }
    for (j = 0; j <= d; j++) { b = 0; for (i = 0; i < N; i++) b += Q[j][i] * g[i]; for (i = 0; i < N; i++) m[i] += b * Q[j][i]; }
    for (i = 0; i < N; i++) mn += m[i]; mn /= N;
    for (i = 0; i < N; i++) s += (m[i] - mn) * (m[i] - mn);
    s = Math.sqrt(s / (N - 1));
    for (i = 0; i < N; i++) m[i] /= s;
    return m;
  }
  function compute() {
    var d = +dEl.value, sg = +sEl.value, i, j, k, s;
    mu = signal(d); Y = [];
    for (i = 0; i < N; i++) Y.push(mu[i] + sg * Z[i]);
    dd = []; for (j = 0; j <= KM; j++) { s = 0; for (i = 0; i < N; i++) s += Q[j][i] * Y[i]; dd.push(s); }
    var yb = 0, sst = 0;
    for (i = 0; i < N; i++) yb += Y[i]; yb /= N;
    for (i = 0; i < N; i++) sst += (Y[i] - yb) * (Y[i] - yb);
    r2 = []; r2a = [];
    var ssr = [];
    for (k = 1, s = 0; k <= KM; k++) { s += dd[k] * dd[k]; r2.push(s / sst); r2a.push(1 - (N - 1) / (N - k - 1) * (1 - s / sst)); ssr.push(sst - s); }
    // Cp = SSR/sigma^2 - n + 2p,  AIC = n log(SSR/n) + 2(p+1),  BIC = n log(SSR/n) + (p+1) log n,
    // with p = k+1 coefficients and sigma^2 taken from the largest model.
    var s2 = ssr[KM - 1] / (N - KM - 1);
    cp = []; aic = []; bic = [];
    for (k = 1; k <= KM; k++) {
      var pk = k + 1, R = ssr[k - 1], fit = N * Math.log(R / N);
      cp.push(R / s2 - N + 2 * pk); aic.push(fit + 2 * (pk + 1)); bic.push(fit + (pk + 1) * Math.log(N));
    }
    kmin = { c: argmin(cp), a: argmin(aic), b: argmin(bic) };
  }
  function argmin(a) { var j = 0; for (var i = 1; i < a.length; i++) if (a[i] < a[j]) j = i; return j + 1; }
  function draw() {
    var d = +dEl.value, k = +kEl.value, i, j;
    document.getElementById('raDv').textContent = d; document.getElementById('raKv').textContent = k;
    document.getElementById('raNzv').textContent = (+sEl.value).toFixed(2);
    c.clearRect(0, 0, W, H);
    c.font = '10px sans-serif'; c.lineWidth = 1;
    // ---- left: the data, the truth, the degree-k fit
    var LX = 34, LY = 12, LW = 250, LH = H - 44, YM = 3.4;
    function LPX(x) { return LX + (x + 1) / 2 * LW; } function LPY(y) { return LY + (1 - (y + YM) / (2 * YM)) * LH; }
    c.strokeStyle = '#eee'; c.beginPath(); c.moveTo(LX, LPY(0)); c.lineTo(LX + LW, LPY(0)); c.stroke();
    c.strokeStyle = '#e6e6e6'; c.strokeRect(LX, LY, LW, LH);
    c.save(); c.beginPath(); c.rect(LX, LY, LW, LH); c.clip();
    var fit = []; for (i = 0; i < N; i++) { var v = 0; for (j = 0; j <= k; j++) v += dd[j] * Q[j][i]; fit.push(v); }
    function line(a, col, w) { c.strokeStyle = col; c.lineWidth = w; c.beginPath(); for (var i = 0; i < N; i++) { var px = LPX(xs[i]), py = LPY(a[i]); i ? c.lineTo(px, py) : c.moveTo(px, py); } c.stroke(); }
    line(mu, '#e74c3c', 2.5); line(fit, '#5b8cff', 2);
    c.fillStyle = 'rgba(44,62,80,0.65)';
    for (i = 0; i < N; i++) { c.beginPath(); c.arc(LPX(xs[i]), LPY(Y[i]), 2.2, 0, 6.2832); c.fill(); }
    c.restore();
    c.fillStyle = '#888'; c.textAlign = 'center'; c.fillText('x', LX + LW / 2, H - 4);
    c.textAlign = 'left'; c.fillStyle = '#e74c3c'; c.fillText('truth: degree ' + d, LX + 5, LY + 12);
    c.fillStyle = '#5b8cff'; c.fillText('fit: degree ' + k, LX + 5, LY + 24);
    // ---- right: R² and adjusted R² against the fitted degree
    var RX = 340, RW = W - RX - 14;
    function RPX(kk) { return RX + (kk - 1) / (KM - 1) * RW; } function RPY(y) { return LY + (1 - y) * LH; }
    c.strokeStyle = '#eee'; c.fillStyle = '#999'; c.textAlign = 'right';
    [0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1].forEach(function (g) { c.beginPath(); c.moveTo(RX, RPY(g)); c.lineTo(RX + RW, RPY(g)); c.stroke(); c.fillText(g.toFixed(2), RX - 4, RPY(g) + 3); });
    c.textAlign = 'center'; c.fillText('k (degree fitted)', RX + RW / 2, H - 4);
    c.save(); c.beginPath(); c.rect(RX, LY, RW, LH); c.clip();
    c.strokeStyle = '#c9ccd2'; c.setLineDash([4, 3]); c.beginPath(); c.moveTo(RPX(d), LY); c.lineTo(RPX(d), LY + LH); c.stroke(); c.setLineDash([]);
    function curve(a, col) { c.strokeStyle = col; c.lineWidth = 2.6; c.beginPath(); for (var i = 0; i < KM; i++) { var px = RPX(i + 1), py = RPY(a[i]); i ? c.lineTo(px, py) : c.moveTo(px, py); } c.stroke(); }
    if (showC) {
      c.setLineDash([5, 3]);
      [[cp, '#c0392b'], [aic, '#e67e22'], [bic, '#7c5cff']].forEach(function (o) {
        var a = o[0], lo = Math.min.apply(null, a), hi = Math.max.apply(null, a), rg = (hi - lo) || 1, q;
        c.strokeStyle = o[1]; c.lineWidth = 1.8; c.beginPath();
        for (var i = 0; i < KM; i++) { q = RPY(0.04 + 0.92 * (a[i] - lo) / rg); i ? c.lineTo(RPX(i + 1), q) : c.moveTo(RPX(i + 1), q); }
        c.stroke();
        c.fillStyle = o[1]; c.beginPath(); c.arc(RPX(argmin(a)), RPY(0.04), 3.2, 0, 6.2832); c.fill();
      });
      c.setLineDash([]);
    }
    curve(r2, '#5b8cff'); curve(r2a, '#27ae60');
    c.strokeStyle = '#bbb'; c.setLineDash([3, 3]); c.beginPath(); c.moveTo(RPX(k), LY); c.lineTo(RPX(k), LY + LH); c.stroke(); c.setLineDash([]);
    c.fillStyle = '#5b8cff'; c.beginPath(); c.arc(RPX(k), RPY(r2[k - 1]), 3.5, 0, 6.2832); c.fill();
    c.fillStyle = '#27ae60'; c.beginPath(); c.arc(RPX(k), RPY(r2a[k - 1]), 3.5, 0, 6.2832); c.fill();
    c.restore();
    c.fillStyle = '#9aa0aa'; c.textAlign = 'center'; c.fillText('d', RPX(d), LY + LH + 12);
    document.getElementById('raR2').textContent = r2[k - 1].toFixed(3);
    document.getElementById('raR2a').textContent = r2a[k - 1].toFixed(3);
    document.getElementById('raKc').textContent = kmin.c; document.getElementById('raKa').textContent = kmin.a;
    document.getElementById('raKb').textContent = kmin.b;
  }
  function save() { try { localStorage.setItem(KEY, JSON.stringify({ d: +dEl.value, k: +kEl.value, s: +sEl.value, c: showC })); } catch (e) {} }
  var cBtn = document.getElementById('raCritBtn');
  function setC(v) { showC = v; cBtn.classList.toggle('on', v); document.getElementById('raCritOut').style.display = v ? '' : 'none'; }
  cBtn.addEventListener('click', function () { setC(!showC); draw(); save(); });
  var st = null; try { st = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(KEY)); } catch (e) {}
  if (st) { if (st.d != null) dEl.value = st.d; if (st.k != null) kEl.value = st.k; if (st.s != null) sEl.value = st.s; }
  kEl.addEventListener('input', function () { draw(); save(); });
  [dEl, sEl].forEach(function (el) { el.addEventListener('input', function () { compute(); draw(); save(); }); });
  document.getElementById('raNew').addEventListener('click', function () { regen(); compute(); draw(); });
  setC(!!(st && st.c));
  regen(); compute(); draw();
})();
</script>
```

# Testing Linear Constraints on β

## Linear Constraints

. . .

We want to test **q linear constraints** on the coefficient vector $\beta \in \mathbb R^p$.

. . .

This is formulated as:

::: {.square-def}
$$H_0: R\beta = 0 \quad \text{vs} \quad H_1: R\beta \neq 0$$

:::


where **R** is a $(q × p)$ constraint matrix encoding the restrictions, with $q \leq p$.

## Common Test Types

. . .


::: {.square-def}
$H_0: R\beta = 0 \quad \text{vs} \quad H_1: R\beta \neq 0$

:::


- **Student's t-test**: is variable $j$ significant? \
[$H_0: \beta_j = 0$ vs $H_1: \beta_j \neq 0$]{style="background-color: lightblue;"}
- **Global F-test**: is any variable significant? Here $R = (0 \mid I_{p-1})$: all slopes, intercept left free \
[$H_0: \beta_2 = \cdots = \beta_p = 0$ vs $H_1: \exists j \in \{2,\ldots,p\}$ s.t. $\beta_j \neq 0$ ]{style="background-color: lightblue;"}
- **Nested model test**: are q variables jointly significant? \
[$H_0: \beta_{p-q+1} = \cdots = \beta_p = 0$ vs $H_1$: the contrary]{style="background-color: lightblue;"}


## Key Applications

- **Individual significance**: Testing if a single predictor matters
- **Overall model significance**: Testing if the model explains anything beyond the intercept  
- **Variable subset significance**: Testing if a group of variables contributes to the model

## Fisher Test

. . .


::: {.callout-note}
## Theorem

- $SSR$: sum of squares of residuals in the unconstrained regression model
- $SSR_c$: sum of squares of residuals in the constrained regression model, i.e., in the sub-model satisfying $R\beta = 0$
  
::: {.fragment}
If $\text{rank}(X) = p$ (with $p < n$), $\text{rank}(R)=q$ and $\varepsilon \sim N(0, \sigma^2 I_n)$, then under $H_0: R\beta = 0$:

$$F = \frac{n-p}{q} \cdot \frac{{SSR}_c - {SSR}}{{SSR}} \sim F(q, n-p)$$

where $F(q, n-p)$ denotes the Fisher distribution with $(q, n-p)$ degrees of freedom. [Elements of proof](../lectures/validation.qmd#F-Test)
:::
:::


## Rejection Region {.smaller}

. . .

Key argument: $SSR_c - SSR = \|(P_{V_0^\perp}-P_{[X]^\perp})Y\|^2 \geq 0$: the squared norm of a projection of $Y$ onto a $q$-dimensional space, where [$V_0=X(Ker(R))$]{style="background-color: lightblue;"} and $\dim(V_0)=p-q$ (so $[X]\ominus V_0$ has dimension $q$).

. . .

Under $H_1$, $F$ tends to be [large]{style="background-color: yellow;"}, so the critical region at significance level $\alpha$ is [one-sided]{style="background-color: yellow;"}:

::: {.square-def}
$$RC_\alpha = \{F > f_{q,n-p}(1-\alpha)\}$$
:::



where $f_{q,n-p}(1-\alpha)$ denotes the $(1-\alpha)$-quantile of an $F(q, n-p)$ distribution.

. . .

p-value: $\P(Z \geq F_{obs})$, where $Z \sim F(q,n-p)$ and $F_{obs}$ is the observed statistic.



## Particular Case 1: Student Test {.smaller}

. . .

Fix some variable $j$ and consider

::: {.square-def}
$H_0: \beta_j=0$ VS $H_1:\beta_j\neq 0$
:::



. . .

Only one constraint: $q=1$, so that

:::{style="font-size: 80%;"}
::: {.square-def}
$$ F = (n-p) \frac{SSR_c-SSR}{SSR} \sim \mathcal F(1,n-p)$$
:::
:::

. . .

$\mathcal F(1,n-p)$ is the distribution of $T^2$ when $T \sim \mathcal T(n-p)$

. . .

In fact, here $F = \big(\tfrac{\hat \beta_j}{\hat \sigma_{\hat \beta_j}}\big)^2$ so [$F$ is the squared student test statistic]{style="background-color: yellow;"} presented before

. . .

Since $f_{1,n-p}(1-\alpha) = t_{n-p}(1-\alpha/2)^2$, rejecting when $F > f_{1,n-p}(1-\alpha)$ is [exactly the two-sided Student test]{style="background-color: yellow;"}


## Particular Case 2: Global Fisher Test {.smaller}

. . .

Assume the model has an [intercept]{style="background-color: yellow;"}: $\1 \in [X]$, say $X^{(1)} = \1$.

. . .

::: {.square-def}
$H_0: \beta_2= \dots = \beta_p=0$ VS $H_1$: contrary
:::

$q = p-1$ in this case

. . .

Constrained model: intercept only, so $SSR_c = \|Y - \overline Y \1\|^2 = SST$ and [$SSR_c - SSR = SST - SSR = SSE$]{style="background-color: lightblue;"}

. . .

::: {.square-def}
$$F = \frac{n-p}{p-1}\frac{SSE}{SSR} = \frac{n-p}{p-1}\frac{R^2}{1-R^2} \sim \mathcal F(p-1, n-p)$$
:::

## Particular Case 3: Nested Fisher Test {.smaller}


. . .

::: {.square-def}
$H_0: \beta_{p-q+1}= \dots = \beta_p=0$ VS $H_1$: contrary
:::


. . .

$SSR_c$: residuals of the [constrained submodel]{style="background-color: lightblue;"} using only the first $p-q$ variables; $SSR$: residuals of the full model

. . .

::: {.square-def}
$$F = \frac{n-p}{q}\frac{SSR_c - SSR}{SSR} \sim \mathcal F(q, n-p)$$
:::

. . .

Interpretation:

If [$F > f_{q,n-p}(1-\alpha)$]{style="background-color: yellow;"} ($1-\alpha$-quantile of Fisher dist.) we reject $H_0$: we [reject the submodel]{style="background-color: yellow;"} in favour of the larger model.

# Verification of Model Hypotheses

## Model Assumptions {.smaller}

. . .


The linear regression model relies on the following key assumptions:

- **Model specification**: $Y = X\beta + \varepsilon$ (linear relationship)
- **Full rank design**: $\text{rank}(X) = p$ (no perfect multicollinearity)
- **Zero mean errors**: $\mathbb{E}(\varepsilon) = 0$
- **Homoscedastic errors**: $\text{Var}(\varepsilon) = \sigma^2 I_n$ (constant variance and uncorrelated errors)

. . .

Now: diagnostic tools to [verify each assumption]{style="background-color: yellow;"} and remedial strategies when they fail.


## Linearity: diagnostic tools

. . .


The linearity assumption $\mathbb{E}(Y) = X\beta$ is the fundamental hypothesis of linear regression.

**Diagnostic Tools:**

- **Pre-modeling**: Scatter plots $(X^{(j)}, Y)$ and empirical correlations for each predictor
- **Post-modeling**: Residual analysis - non-linearity manifests as patterns in $\hat{\varepsilon}$
- **Advanced**: Partial residual plots (not covered here)

## Linearity: remedies

. . .


The linearity assumption $\mathbb{E}(Y) = X\beta$ is the fundamental hypothesis of linear regression.

**Remedial Strategies:**

- **Transformations**: Apply transformations to $Y$ and/or predictors $X^{(j)}$ to achieve linearity
- **Alternative models**: If transformations fail, consider nonlinear regression models

## log X straightens the curve {.smaller}

::: {style="font-size:86%"}
Truth: $Y = 1 + 2\log X + \varepsilon$, fitted by a **straight line** in the chosen scale. Raw $X$: the residuals [curve]{style="background-color: yellow;"} and the nested $F$-test for an added $u^2$ rejects. On $\log X$: [structureless]{style="background-color: lightgreen;"}, and the test stops rejecting.
:::

```{=html}
<style>
.lm-btn{font-family:inherit;font-size:.85em;padding:.4em 1.1em;margin:.12em .22em;border:1px solid #bbb;border-radius:8px;background:#f4f4f4;color:#333;cursor:pointer}
.lm-btn.on{background:#3b6fb6;color:#fff;border-color:#3b6fb6}
.lm-row{font-size:.72em;line-height:2.3;margin:.12rem 0}
.lm-wrap{text-align:center}
</style>
<div class="lm-wrap" id="scWrap">
  <canvas id="scCanvas" width="620" height="270" style="background:#fff;border:1px solid #ddd;border-radius:8px;max-width:100%"></canvas>
  <div class="lm-row">
    fit against <button class="lm-btn on" data-u="id">X</button><button class="lm-btn" data-u="sqrt">&radic;X</button><button class="lm-btn" data-u="log">log X</button>
    &nbsp; noise &sigma; <input id="scNz" type="range" autocomplete="off" min="0.1" max="1" step="0.05" value="0.5" style="vertical-align:middle;width:90px"> <b id="scNzv">0.50</b> &nbsp; <button class="lm-btn" id="scNew">&#8635; resample</button>
  </div>
  <div class="lm-row">curvature test, add \(u^2\): &nbsp; F = <b id="scF">&ndash;</b> &nbsp; p = <b id="scP">&ndash;</b> &nbsp;&middot;&nbsp; <span style="color:#c0392b">bars</span> = mean residual per third of the fitted range</div>
</div>
<script>
(function () {
  var cv = document.getElementById('scCanvas'); if (!cv || cv.dataset.init) return; cv.dataset.init = 1;
  var c = cv.getContext('2d'), W = cv.width, H = cv.height, N = 60, KEY = 'lmStraighten';
  var mode = 'id', Xr = [], Z = [], nzEl = document.getElementById('scNz');
  var LAB = { id: 'X', sqrt: '√X', log: 'log X' };
  function gauss() { var u = 0, v = 0; while (!u) u = Math.random(); while (!v) v = Math.random(); return Math.sqrt(-2 * Math.log(u)) * Math.cos(2 * Math.PI * v); }
  function regen() { Xr = []; Z = []; for (var i = 0; i < N; i++) { Xr.push(0.3 + 9.7 * Math.random()); Z.push(gauss()); } }
  // same p-value machinery as the correlation test in the introduction deck
  function lgamma(z) { var g = [0.99999999999980993, 676.5203681218851, -1259.1392167224028, 771.32342877765313, -176.61502916214059, 12.507343278686905, -0.13857109526572012, 9.9843695780195716e-6, 1.5056327351493116e-7]; if (z < 0.5) return Math.log(Math.PI / Math.sin(Math.PI * z)) - lgamma(1 - z); z -= 1; var x = g[0]; for (var i = 1; i < 9; i++) x += g[i] / (z + i); var t = z + 7.5; return 0.5 * Math.log(2 * Math.PI) + (z + 0.5) * Math.log(t) - t + Math.log(x); }
  function betacf(a, b, x) { var FPMIN = 1e-300, qab = a + b, qap = a + 1, qam = a - 1, cc = 1, d = 1 - qab * x / qap; if (Math.abs(d) < FPMIN) d = FPMIN; d = 1 / d; var h = d; for (var m = 1; m <= 200; m++) { var m2 = 2 * m, aa = m * (b - m) * x / ((qam + m2) * (a + m2)); d = 1 + aa * d; if (Math.abs(d) < FPMIN) d = FPMIN; cc = 1 + aa / cc; if (Math.abs(cc) < FPMIN) cc = FPMIN; d = 1 / d; h *= d * cc; aa = -(a + m) * (qab + m) * x / ((a + m2) * (qap + m2)); d = 1 + aa * d; if (Math.abs(d) < FPMIN) d = FPMIN; cc = 1 + aa / cc; if (Math.abs(cc) < FPMIN) cc = FPMIN; d = 1 / d; var del = d * cc; h *= del; if (Math.abs(del - 1) < 3e-12) break; } return h; }
  function betai(a, b, x) { if (x <= 0) return 0; if (x >= 1) return 1; var bt = Math.exp(lgamma(a + b) - lgamma(a) - lgamma(b) + a * Math.log(x) + b * Math.log(1 - x)); return x < (a + 1) / (a + b + 2) ? bt * betacf(a, b, x) / a : 1 - bt * betacf(b, a, 1 - x) / b; }
  function pf(F, d1, d2) { return F <= 0 ? 1 : betai(d2 / 2, d1 / 2, d2 / (d2 + d1 * F)); }   // P(F_{d1,d2} > F)
  function draw() {
    var i, sg = +nzEl.value;
    document.getElementById('scNzv').textContent = sg.toFixed(2);
    var u = [], Y = [];
    for (i = 0; i < N; i++) {
      u.push(mode === 'log' ? Math.log(Xr[i]) : mode === 'sqrt' ? Math.sqrt(Xr[i]) : Xr[i]);
      Y.push(1 + 2 * Math.log(Xr[i]) + sg * Z[i]);
    }
    // orthonormalise [1, u, u^2] (Gram-Schmidt): the projections then give every SSR
    var q0 = [], q1 = [], q2 = [], a, s;
    for (i = 0; i < N; i++) q0.push(1 / Math.sqrt(N));
    a = 0; for (i = 0; i < N; i++) a += u[i] * q0[i];
    s = 0; for (i = 0; i < N; i++) { q1.push(u[i] - a * q0[i]); s += q1[i] * q1[i]; }
    s = Math.sqrt(s); for (i = 0; i < N; i++) q1[i] /= s;
    var b0 = 0, b1 = 0; for (i = 0; i < N; i++) { b0 += u[i] * u[i] * q0[i]; b1 += u[i] * u[i] * q1[i]; }
    s = 0; for (i = 0; i < N; i++) { q2.push(u[i] * u[i] - b0 * q0[i] - b1 * q1[i]); s += q2[i] * q2[i]; }
    s = Math.sqrt(s); for (i = 0; i < N; i++) q2[i] /= s;
    var c0 = 0, c1 = 0, c2 = 0, yy = 0;
    for (i = 0; i < N; i++) { c0 += Y[i] * q0[i]; c1 += Y[i] * q1[i]; c2 += Y[i] * q2[i]; yy += Y[i] * Y[i]; }
    var ssr2 = yy - c0 * c0 - c1 * c1, ssr3 = ssr2 - c2 * c2;
    var F = c2 * c2 / (ssr3 / (N - 3)), pv = pf(F, 1, N - 3);
    var fit = [], res = [];
    for (i = 0; i < N; i++) { fit.push(c0 * q0[i] + c1 * q1[i]); res.push(Y[i] - fit[i]); }
    var umin = 1e9, umax = -1e9, ymin = 1e9, ymax = -1e9, rmax = 1e-9, fmin = 1e9, fmax = -1e9;
    for (i = 0; i < N; i++) {
      if (u[i] < umin) umin = u[i]; if (u[i] > umax) umax = u[i];
      if (Y[i] < ymin) ymin = Y[i]; if (Y[i] > ymax) ymax = Y[i];
      if (Math.abs(res[i]) > rmax) rmax = Math.abs(res[i]);
      if (fit[i] < fmin) fmin = fit[i]; if (fit[i] > fmax) fmax = fit[i];
    }
    c.clearRect(0, 0, W, H); c.font = '11px sans-serif'; c.lineWidth = 1;
    var gap = 26, pw = (W - gap) / 2, ph = H - 34, top = 8;
    // ---- left: the data on the chosen scale, with the least-squares LINE
    var lx0 = 30, lx1 = pw - 6, ux = (umax - umin) * 0.06 + 1e-9, uy = (ymax - ymin) * 0.08;
    function LX(v) { return lx0 + (v - umin + ux) / ((umax - umin) + 2 * ux) * (lx1 - lx0); }
    function LY(v) { return top + (ymax + uy - v) / ((ymax - ymin) + 2 * uy) * ph; }
    c.strokeStyle = '#e6e6e6'; c.strokeRect(lx0, top, lx1 - lx0, ph);
    c.fillStyle = '#777'; c.textAlign = 'center'; c.fillText('(' + LAB[mode] + ', Y) + line', (lx0 + lx1) / 2, H - 6);
    c.save(); c.beginPath(); c.rect(lx0, top, lx1 - lx0, ph); c.clip();
    var ord = []; for (i = 0; i < N; i++) ord.push(i);
    ord.sort(function (p, q) { return u[p] - u[q]; });
    c.strokeStyle = '#e74c3c'; c.lineWidth = 2; c.beginPath();
    for (i = 0; i < N; i++) { var j = ord[i]; i ? c.lineTo(LX(u[j]), LY(fit[j])) : c.moveTo(LX(u[j]), LY(fit[j])); }
    c.stroke();
    c.fillStyle = 'rgba(44,62,80,0.7)';
    for (i = 0; i < N; i++) { c.beginPath(); c.arc(LX(u[i]), LY(Y[i]), 2.4, 0, 6.2832); c.fill(); }
    c.restore();
    // ---- right: residuals vs fitted, with the mean residual of each third
    var rx0 = pw + gap, rx1 = W - 10, fp = (fmax - fmin) * 0.07 + 1e-9;
    function RX(v) { return rx0 + (v - fmin + fp) / ((fmax - fmin) + 2 * fp) * (rx1 - rx0); }
    function RY(v) { return top + (rmax * 1.2 - v) / (2.4 * rmax) * ph; }
    c.strokeStyle = '#e6e6e6'; c.strokeRect(rx0, top, rx1 - rx0, ph);
    c.fillStyle = '#777'; c.textAlign = 'center'; c.fillText('residuals vs fitted', (rx0 + rx1) / 2, H - 6);
    c.save(); c.beginPath(); c.rect(rx0, top, rx1 - rx0, ph); c.clip();
    c.strokeStyle = '#aaa'; c.setLineDash([4, 3]); c.beginPath(); c.moveTo(rx0, RY(0)); c.lineTo(rx1, RY(0)); c.stroke(); c.setLineDash([]);
    for (var t = 0; t < 3; t++) {
      var lo = fmin + (fmax - fmin) * t / 3, hi = fmin + (fmax - fmin) * (t + 1) / 3, m = 0, n = 0;
      for (i = 0; i < N; i++) if (fit[i] >= lo && (fit[i] < hi || t === 2)) { m += res[i]; n++; }
      if (!n) continue;
      m /= n; c.strokeStyle = '#c0392b'; c.lineWidth = 2.6; c.beginPath();
      c.moveTo(RX(lo) + 3, RY(m)); c.lineTo(RX(hi) - 3, RY(m)); c.stroke();
    }
    c.fillStyle = 'rgba(44,62,80,0.7)';
    for (i = 0; i < N; i++) { c.beginPath(); c.arc(RX(fit[i]), RY(res[i]), 2.4, 0, 6.2832); c.fill(); }
    c.restore();
    document.getElementById('scF').textContent = F.toFixed(1);
    var pEl = document.getElementById('scP');
    pEl.textContent = pv < 0.001 ? '< 0.001' : pv.toFixed(3);
    pEl.style.color = pv < 0.05 ? '#c0392b' : '#27ae60';
  }
  function save() { try { localStorage.setItem(KEY, JSON.stringify({ u: mode, s: +nzEl.value })); } catch (e) {} }
  function setMode(m) {
    mode = m;
    Array.prototype.forEach.call(document.querySelectorAll('#scWrap .lm-btn[data-u]'), function (b) { b.classList.toggle('on', b.dataset.u === m); });
    draw(); save();
  }
  Array.prototype.forEach.call(document.querySelectorAll('#scWrap .lm-btn[data-u]'), function (b) {
    b.addEventListener('click', function () { setMode(b.dataset.u); });
  });
  nzEl.addEventListener('input', function () { draw(); save(); });
  document.getElementById('scNew').addEventListener('click', function () { regen(); draw(); });
  var st = null; try { st = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(KEY)); } catch (e) {}
  if (st && st.s != null) nzEl.value = st.s;
  regen(); setMode(st && LAB[st.u] ? st.u : 'id');
})();
</script>
```

## Full rank: why it matters

. . .


The condition $\text{rank}(X) = p$ ensures no predictor $X^{(j)}$ is a linear combination of others.

. . .

**Why it matters:**

- **Identifiability**: Without full rank, $\beta$ is not uniquely defined
- **Estimation**: $(X^TX)$ becomes non-invertible, making $\hat{\beta} = (X^TX)^{-1}X^TY$ undefined
 - Infinitely many solutions satisfy $X^TX\hat{\beta} = X^TY$

## Full rank: in practice

. . .


The condition $\text{rank}(X) = p$ ensures no predictor $X^{(j)}$ is a linear combination of others.

**In practice:**

- Perfect collinearity is rare, so $\text{rank}(X) = p$ usually holds
- **Near-collinearity** is the real concern - when predictors are "almost" linearly dependent

## Near-collinearity: consequences

. . .


When a variable is highly correlated with others (correlation close to but not exactly $\pm 1$):

. . .

**Mathematical consequences:**

- $X^TX$ remains invertible, but its smallest eigenvalue approaches zero
- $(X^TX)^{-1}$ becomes numerically unstable

## Near-collinearity: instability

. . .

**Statistical implications:**

- **Instability**: Adding/removing a single observation can drastically change $(X^TX)^{-1}$
- **Unreliable estimates**: $\hat{\beta} = (X^TX)^{-1}X^TY$ becomes highly unstable
- **Inflated variance**: $\text{Var}(\hat{\beta}) = \sigma^2(X^TX)^{-1}$ becomes very large

. . .

This is undesirable from a statistical point of view

## Collinearity in 3D: the cloud collapses {.smaller}

::: {style="font-size:86%"}
One dot per observation $(X^{(1)}_i, X^{(2)}_i, Y_i)$, grey = its shadow on the floor. At $r=1$ the shadow is a [line]{style="background-color: yellow;"} and the plane [tilts for free]{style="background-color: orange;"}.
:::

```{=html}
<style>
.lm-btn{font-family:inherit;font-size:.85em;padding:.4em 1.1em;margin:.12em .22em;border:1px solid #bbb;border-radius:8px;background:#f4f4f4;color:#333;cursor:pointer}
.lm-row{font-size:.72em;line-height:2.3;margin:.12rem 0}
.lm-wrap{text-align:center}
</style>
<div class="lm-wrap" id="c3Wrap">
  <canvas id="c3Canvas" width="700" height="300" style="background:#fff;border:1px solid #ddd;border-radius:8px;max-width:100%;touch-action:none;cursor:grab"></canvas>
  <div class="lm-row">
    collinearity r <input id="c3R" type="range" autocomplete="off" min="0" max="1" step="0.01" value="0.5" style="vertical-align:middle;width:150px"> <b id="c3Rv">0.50</b>
    &nbsp;·&nbsp; tilt the plane <input id="c3P" type="range" autocomplete="off" min="-1" max="1" step="0.02" value="0" style="vertical-align:middle;width:120px">
    &nbsp; <button class="lm-btn" id="c3New">&#8635; resample</button>
  </div>
  <div class="lm-row">VIF = 1/(1&minus;r²) = <b id="c3V">&ndash;</b> &nbsp;·&nbsp; tilting costs <b id="c3D">&ndash;</b> of SSR (minimum <b id="c3S">&ndash;</b>)</div>
</div>
<script>
(function () {
  var cv = document.getElementById('c3Canvas'); if (!cv || cv.dataset.init) return; cv.dataset.init = 1;
  var c = cv.getContext('2d'), W = cv.width, H = cv.height, N = 60, SG = 0.6, KEY = 'lmColl3D';
  var z1 = [], z2 = [], Ez = [], yaw = 0.55, drag = null;
  var rEl = document.getElementById('c3R'), pEl = document.getElementById('c3P');
  var AX = 3, TILT = 1.2, FP = 0.78, SC = 108, VS = 88, SP = 0.42, CX = W / 2, CY = H / 2 + 14;
  function gauss() { var u = 0, v = 0; while (!u) u = Math.random(); while (!v) v = Math.random(); return Math.sqrt(-2 * Math.log(u)) * Math.cos(2 * Math.PI * v); }
  function regen() { z1 = []; z2 = []; Ez = []; for (var i = 0; i < N; i++) { z1.push(gauss()); z2.push(gauss()); Ez.push(gauss()); } }
  function pos(e) { var b = cv.getBoundingClientRect(); return [(e.clientX - b.left) * W / b.width, (e.clientY - b.top) * H / b.height]; }
  function draw() {
    var i, r = +rEl.value, tl = +pEl.value * TILT;
    document.getElementById('c3Rv').textContent = r.toFixed(2);
    // r = 1 makes X2 identical to X1, so the design really is rank-deficient here
    var x1 = [], x2 = [], Y = [], rt = Math.sqrt(1 - r * r), m1 = 0, m2 = 0, my = 0;
    for (i = 0; i < N; i++) {
      x1.push(z1[i]); x2.push(r * z1[i] + rt * z2[i]);
      Y.push(1 + x1[i] + x2[i] + SG * Ez[i]);
      m1 += x1[i]; m2 += x2[i]; my += Y[i];
    }
    m1 /= N; m2 /= N; my /= N;
    var s11 = 0, s22 = 0, s12 = 0, s1y = 0, s2y = 0, nv = 0;
    for (i = 0; i < N; i++) {
      var a = x1[i] - m1, b = x2[i] - m2, g = Y[i] - my;
      s11 += a * a; s22 += b * b; s12 += a * b; s1y += a * g; s2y += b * g;
      nv += Math.pow((a - b) / Math.SQRT2, 2);          // v = (1,-1)/√2: the null direction at r = 1
    }
    var det = s11 * s22 - s12 * s12, B1, B2;
    if (det > 1e-9) { B1 = (s22 * s1y - s12 * s2y) / det; B2 = (s11 * s2y - s12 * s1y) / det; }
    else { var g0 = s1y / s11; B1 = g0 / 2; B2 = g0 / 2; }   // singular: any b1+b2 = g0 fits equally well
    var b1 = B1 + tl / Math.SQRT2, b2 = B2 - tl / Math.SQRT2, b0 = my - b1 * m1 - b2 * m2;
    var ssr0 = 0;
    for (i = 0; i < N; i++) { var f0 = my - B1 * m1 - B2 * m2 + B1 * x1[i] + B2 * x2[i]; ssr0 += (Y[i] - f0) * (Y[i] - f0); }
    var dssr = tl * tl * nv;
    // the smaller eigenvalue of the centred design: how thick the cloud is across its line
    var tr = (s11 + s22) / 2, dv = Math.sqrt((s11 - s22) * (s11 - s22) / 4 + s12 * s12);
    var thick = Math.sqrt(Math.max(0, tr - dv) / N);
    var ylo = 1e9, yhi = -1e9;
    for (i = 0; i < N; i++) { if (Y[i] < ylo) ylo = Y[i]; if (Y[i] > yhi) yhi = Y[i]; }
    var pad = (yhi - ylo) * 0.12; ylo -= pad; yhi += pad;
    function Wof(y) { return 2 * (y - ylo) / (yhi - ylo) - 1; }          // data height -> [-1,1]
    function PR(u, v, w) {                                               // box coords -> screen
      var ex = u * Math.cos(yaw) - v * Math.sin(yaw), ey = u * Math.sin(yaw) + v * Math.cos(yaw);
      return [CX + SC * ex, CY + SC * ey * SP - VS * w];
    }
    function PT(a, b, y) { return PR(a / AX, b / AX, Wof(y)); }
    c.clearRect(0, 0, W, H); c.font = '11px sans-serif';
    // ---- the box: floor, uprights, lid
    var fl = [[-1, -1], [1, -1], [1, 1], [-1, 1]];
    c.strokeStyle = '#d4d4d4'; c.lineWidth = 1; c.beginPath();
    for (i = 0; i < 4; i++) { var p = PR(fl[i][0], fl[i][1], -1), q = PR(fl[(i + 1) % 4][0], fl[(i + 1) % 4][1], -1); i ? c.lineTo(q[0], q[1]) : (c.moveTo(p[0], p[1]), c.lineTo(q[0], q[1])); }
    c.closePath(); c.stroke();
    c.strokeStyle = '#ececec'; c.beginPath();
    for (i = 0; i < 4; i++) { var lo = PR(fl[i][0], fl[i][1], -1), hi = PR(fl[i][0], fl[i][1], 1); c.moveTo(lo[0], lo[1]); c.lineTo(hi[0], hi[1]); }
    for (i = 0; i < 4; i++) { var t1 = PR(fl[i][0], fl[i][1], 1), t2 = PR(fl[(i + 1) % 4][0], fl[(i + 1) % 4][1], 1); c.moveTo(t1[0], t1[1]); c.lineTo(t2[0], t2[1]); }
    c.stroke();
    // floor grid
    c.strokeStyle = '#efefef'; c.beginPath();
    for (i = -2; i <= 2; i++) {
      var ga = PR(i / 2, -1, -1), gb = PR(i / 2, 1, -1), gc = PR(-1, i / 2, -1), gd = PR(1, i / 2, -1);
      c.moveTo(ga[0], ga[1]); c.lineTo(gb[0], gb[1]); c.moveTo(gc[0], gc[1]); c.lineTo(gd[0], gd[1]);
    }
    c.stroke();
    // ---- the fitted plane, clipped to the box (w in [-1,1]) by Sutherland-Hodgman
    var poly = [[-FP, -FP], [FP, -FP], [FP, FP], [-FP, FP]];
    function wAt(u, v) { return Wof(b0 + b1 * u * AX + b2 * v * AX); }
    function clip(pl, keepUpper) {
      var out = [], n = pl.length, k;
      function f(p) { var w = wAt(p[0], p[1]); return keepUpper ? 1 - w : w + 1; }   // >= 0 stays
      for (k = 0; k < n; k++) {
        var A = pl[k], B = pl[(k + 1) % n], fa = f(A), fb = f(B);
        if (fa >= 0) out.push(A);
        if ((fa >= 0) !== (fb >= 0)) { var t = fa / (fa - fb); out.push([A[0] + t * (B[0] - A[0]), A[1] + t * (B[1] - A[1])]); }
      }
      return out;
    }
    poly = clip(clip(poly, true), false);
    if (poly.length > 2) {
      c.beginPath();
      for (i = 0; i < poly.length; i++) { var pp = PR(poly[i][0], poly[i][1], wAt(poly[i][0], poly[i][1])); i ? c.lineTo(pp[0], pp[1]) : c.moveTo(pp[0], pp[1]); }
      c.closePath();
      c.fillStyle = 'rgba(52,152,219,0.20)'; c.fill();
      c.strokeStyle = '#3b6fb6'; c.lineWidth = 1.6; c.stroke();
    }
    // ---- shadows on the floor, stems, then the points (far ones first)
    var ord = []; for (i = 0; i < N; i++) ord.push(i);
    ord.sort(function (p, q) { return (x1[q] * Math.sin(yaw) + x2[q] * Math.cos(yaw)) - (x1[p] * Math.sin(yaw) + x2[p] * Math.cos(yaw)); });
    c.strokeStyle = 'rgba(0,0,0,0.07)'; c.lineWidth = 1; c.beginPath();
    for (i = 0; i < N; i++) { var j = ord[i], sh = PR(x1[j] / AX, x2[j] / AX, -1), pt = PT(x1[j], x2[j], Y[j]); c.moveTo(sh[0], sh[1]); c.lineTo(pt[0], pt[1]); }
    c.stroke();
    c.fillStyle = 'rgba(120,128,140,0.55)';
    for (i = 0; i < N; i++) { var j2 = ord[i], s2 = PR(x1[j2] / AX, x2[j2] / AX, -1); c.beginPath(); c.arc(s2[0], s2[1], 2.1, 0, 6.2832); c.fill(); }
    // the shadow's own two axes, each one standard deviation long: the short one is the thickness
    var lmax = tr + dv, ev = Math.hypot(s12, lmax - s11);
    var e1 = ev > 1e-9 ? [s12 / ev, (lmax - s11) / ev] : [1, 0], e2 = [-e1[1], e1[0]];
    [[e1, Math.sqrt(lmax / N), '#5b8cff', 2.2], [e2, thick, '#c0392b', 2.6]].forEach(function (o) {
      var d = o[0], L = o[1], pA = PR((m1 - d[0] * L) / AX, (m2 - d[1] * L) / AX, -1), pB = PR((m1 + d[0] * L) / AX, (m2 + d[1] * L) / AX, -1);
      c.strokeStyle = o[2]; c.lineWidth = o[3]; c.beginPath(); c.moveTo(pA[0], pA[1]); c.lineTo(pB[0], pB[1]); c.stroke();
    });
    for (i = 0; i < N; i++) {
      var j3 = ord[i], p3 = PT(x1[j3], x2[j3], Y[j3]);
      c.fillStyle = 'rgba(44,62,80,0.82)'; c.beginPath(); c.arc(p3[0], p3[1], 2.8, 0, 6.2832); c.fill();
    }
    // ---- axis labels
    c.fillStyle = '#8a9099'; c.textAlign = 'center';
    var la = PR(1.14, -1, -1), lb = PR(-1, 1.14, -1), lc = PR(-1, -1, 1);
    c.fillText('X₁', la[0], la[1] + 4); c.fillText('X₂', lb[0], lb[1] + 4); c.fillText('Y', lc[0] - 11, lc[1] - 3);

    var vEl = document.getElementById('c3V');
    vEl.textContent = r >= 1 ? '∞' : (1 / (1 - r * r)).toFixed(1);
    var dEl = document.getElementById('c3D');
    dEl.textContent = dssr.toFixed(4);
    dEl.style.color = Math.abs(tl) > 0.1 && dssr < 0.01 * ssr0 ? '#c0392b' : '#333';
    document.getElementById('c3S').textContent = ssr0.toFixed(3);
  }
  function save() { try { localStorage.setItem(KEY, JSON.stringify({ r: +rEl.value, p: +pEl.value, y: yaw })); } catch (e) {} }
  cv.addEventListener('pointerdown', function (e) { drag = pos(e)[0]; cv.style.cursor = 'grabbing'; });
  window.addEventListener('pointerup', function () { if (drag !== null) { drag = null; cv.style.cursor = 'grab'; save(); } });
  cv.addEventListener('pointermove', function (e) {
    if (drag === null) return;
    var x = pos(e)[0]; yaw += (x - drag) * 0.012; drag = x; draw(); e.preventDefault();
  });
  [rEl, pEl].forEach(function (el) { el.addEventListener('input', function () { draw(); save(); }); });
  document.getElementById('c3New').addEventListener('click', function () { regen(); draw(); });
  var st = null; try { st = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(KEY)); } catch (e) {}
  if (st) { if (st.r != null) rEl.value = st.r; if (st.p != null) pEl.value = st.p; if (st.y != null) yaw = st.y; }
  regen(); draw();
})();
</script>
```

## Detecting Collinearity: VIF {.smaller}

. . .


Compute the VIF (Variance Inflation Factor) for each $X^{(j)}$:

1. Regress $X^{(j)}$ on all other $X^{(k)}$ (where $k \neq j$)
2. Compute $R_j^2$ from this regression
3. Calculate: $\text{VIF}_j = \frac{1}{1 - R_j^2}$

. . .

**Properties:**

- $\text{VIF}_j \geq 1$ always
- High VIF indicates collinearity. Common threshold: [$\text{VIF}_j \geq 5$]{style="background-color: yellow;"}. In R: `vif()` from `car` package


## VIF explodes near collinearity {.smaller}

. . .


::: {style="font-size:86%"}
Regress $X^{(2)}$ on $X^{(1)}$ (left): its $R_2^2$ rises with the correlation, and $\mathrm{VIF}_2=\dfrac{1}{1-R_2^2}$ (right) blows up — inflating $\mathrm{Var}(\hat\beta_2)$ by the same factor.
:::

```{=html}
<style>
.lm-btn{font-family:inherit;font-size:.85em;padding:.4em 1.1em;margin:.12em .22em;border:1px solid #bbb;border-radius:8px;background:#f4f4f4;color:#333;cursor:pointer}
.lm-row{font-size:.72em;line-height:2.3;margin:.12rem 0}
.lm-wrap{text-align:center}
</style>
<div class="lm-wrap">
  <canvas id="vfCanvas" width="600" height="280" style="background:#fff;border:1px solid #ddd;border-radius:8px;max-width:100%"></canvas>
  <div class="lm-row">correlation r (X₁,X₂) <input id="vfR" type="range" autocomplete="off" min="0" max="0.99" step="0.01" value="0.5" style="vertical-align:middle;width:170px"> <b id="vfRv">0.50</b> &nbsp; <button class="lm-btn" id="vfNew">↻ resample</button></div>
  <div class="lm-row">R₂² = <b id="vfR2">–</b> &nbsp;·&nbsp; VIF₂ = 1/(1−R₂²) = <b id="vfVIF">–</b> &nbsp;·&nbsp; <span id="vfMsg">–</span></div>
</div>
<script>
(function () {
  var cv = document.getElementById('vfCanvas'); if (!cv || cv.dataset.init) return; cv.dataset.init = 1;
  var c = cv.getContext('2d'), W = cv.width, H = cv.height, N = 40, z1 = [], z2 = [];
  var rEl = document.getElementById('vfR');
  function gauss() { var u = 0, v = 0; while (!u) u = Math.random(); while (!v) v = Math.random(); return Math.sqrt(-2 * Math.log(u)) * Math.cos(2 * Math.PI * v); }
  function regen() { z1 = []; z2 = []; for (var i = 0; i < N; i++) { z1.push(gauss()); z2.push(gauss()); } }
  function draw() {
    var r = +rEl.value, s = Math.sqrt(1 - r * r), i; document.getElementById('vfRv').textContent = r.toFixed(2);
    var X1 = [], X2 = []; for (i = 0; i < N; i++) { X1.push(z1[i]); X2.push(r * z1[i] + s * z2[i]); }
    var m1 = 0, m2 = 0; for (i = 0; i < N; i++) { m1 += X1[i]; m2 += X2[i]; } m1 /= N; m2 /= N;
    var sxy = 0, sxx = 0, syy = 0; for (i = 0; i < N; i++) { sxy += (X1[i] - m1) * (X2[i] - m2); sxx += (X1[i] - m1) * (X1[i] - m1); syy += (X2[i] - m2) * (X2[i] - m2); }
    var R2 = sxy * sxy / ((sxx * syy) || 1e-9), VIF = 1 / Math.max(1e-6, 1 - R2), b1 = sxy / (sxx || 1e-9), b0 = m2 - b1 * m1;
    c.clearRect(0, 0, W, H); var gap = 26, pw = (W - gap) / 2, ph = H - 30, top = 8;
    // left: scatter X1 vs X2 + regression line
    var lx0 = 28, lx1 = pw - 6, V = 3; function LX(x) { return lx0 + (x + V) / (2 * V) * (lx1 - lx0); } function LY(y) { return top + (V - y) / (2 * V) * ph; }
    c.strokeStyle = '#ddd'; c.strokeRect(lx0, top, lx1 - lx0, ph); c.fillStyle = '#777'; c.font = '11px sans-serif'; c.textAlign = 'center'; c.fillText('X₂ vs X₁  (R₂²)', (lx0 + lx1) / 2, H - 8);
    c.strokeStyle = '#e74c3c'; c.lineWidth = 2; c.beginPath(); c.moveTo(LX(-V), LY(b0 + b1 * (-V))); c.lineTo(LX(V), LY(b0 + b1 * V)); c.stroke();
    c.fillStyle = 'rgba(44,62,80,0.7)'; for (i = 0; i < N; i++) { c.beginPath(); c.arc(LX(X1[i]), LY(X2[i]), 2.8, 0, 6.2832); c.fill(); }
    // right: VIF curve vs r
    var rx0 = pw + gap, rx1 = W - 12, VM = 25; function RX(rr) { return rx0 + rr * (rx1 - rx0); } function RY(v) { return top + (1 - Math.min(v, VM) / VM) * ph; }
    c.strokeStyle = '#ddd'; c.strokeRect(rx0, top, rx1 - rx0, ph); c.fillStyle = '#777'; c.fillText('VIF vs r', (rx0 + rx1) / 2, H - 8);
    c.fillStyle = '#999'; c.font = '9px sans-serif'; c.textAlign = 'right'; [1, 5, 10, 25].forEach(function (g) { c.fillText(g, rx0 - 2, RY(g) + 3); c.strokeStyle = g === 5 ? '#f0c040' : '#eee'; c.beginPath(); c.moveTo(rx0, RY(g)); c.lineTo(rx1, RY(g)); c.stroke(); });
    c.strokeStyle = '#7c5cff'; c.lineWidth = 2.5; c.beginPath(); for (i = 0; i <= 100; i++) { var rr = i / 100 * 0.99, vv = 1 / Math.max(1e-6, 1 - rr * rr); i ? c.lineTo(RX(rr), RY(vv)) : c.moveTo(RX(rr), RY(vv)); } c.stroke();
    c.fillStyle = '#7c5cff'; c.beginPath(); c.arc(RX(Math.sqrt(R2)), RY(VIF), 4.5, 0, 6.2832); c.fill();   // empirical correlation -> point sits on the 1/(1-x^2) curve
    document.getElementById('vfR2').textContent = R2.toFixed(3); document.getElementById('vfVIF').textContent = VIF.toFixed(1);
    document.getElementById('vfMsg').innerHTML = VIF >= 5 ? '<span style="color:#e74c3c">VIF ≥ 5 → collinearity concern</span>' : '<span style="color:#1b7a3a">acceptable</span>';
  }
  rEl.addEventListener('input', draw);
  document.getElementById('vfNew').addEventListener('click', function () { regen(); draw(); });
  regen(); draw();
})();
</script>
```

## Remedies for Multicollinearity {.smaller}

- **Variable removal**: [Drop variables]{style="background-color: yellow;"} with high VIF
 - Preferably remove those [least correlated with $Y$]{style="background-color: yellow;"}
- **Penalized regression**: Ridge, LASSO, or elastic net methods (not covered here)

. . .

**Important Distinction on Multicollinearity**

- **Parameter estimation**: Multicollinearity severely affects $\hat{\beta}$ reliability
- **Prediction**: Not problematic: $\hat{Y}$ remains well-defined and stable since [projection on $[X]$ is still unique]{style="background-color: yellow;"}


## Analysis of the Residuals

. . .

Recall that [$\hat \varepsilon = Y - \widehat Y = P_{[X]^{\perp}} \varepsilon$]{style="background-color: lightblue;"}

. . .

### Residual Properties

- $\E(\hat{\varepsilon}) = 0$
- $\Var(\hat{\varepsilon}) = \sigma^2P_{[X]}^{\perp}$
- $\text{Cov}(\hat{\varepsilon}, \hat{Y}) = 0$
- If $\1 \in [X]$: $\bar{\hat{\varepsilon}} = 0$

## Diagnostic Tools

1. **Graphical Assessment:** Visual evaluation of model quality

2. **Homoscedasticity Test:**
Test: $\Var(\varepsilon_i) = \sigma^2$ for all $i$ (constant variance)
3. **Non-correlation Test:**  
Test: $\Var(\varepsilon)$ is diagonal (uncorrelated errors)

4. **Normality Test:** Examine normality of residuals



## Residual vs. Fitted Plot

. . .

The [scatter plot between $\hat{Y}$ and $\hat{\varepsilon}$]{style="background-color: yellow;"} is informative.

Since $\text{Cov}(\hat{\varepsilon}, \hat{Y}) = 0$, [no structure should appear]{style="background-color: yellow;"}.

If patterns emerge, this may indicate violations of:

- Linearity assumption
- Homoscedasticity assumption  
- Non-correlation assumption
- Or a combination of these...

## Residual vs fitted: read the pattern {.smaller}

. . .


::: {style="font-size:86%"}
Left: data $(x,Y)$ with the **linear** fit. Right: the **residuals vs fitted** plot. When the model is right it's a structureless cloud; a **curve** signals non-linearity, a **funnel** signals heteroscedasticity.
:::

```{=html}
<style>
.lm-btn{font-family:inherit;font-size:.85em;padding:.4em 1.1em;margin:.12em .22em;border:1px solid #bbb;border-radius:8px;background:#f4f4f4;color:#333;cursor:pointer}
.lm-btn.on{background:#3b6fb6;color:#fff;border-color:#3b6fb6}
.lm-row{font-size:.72em;line-height:2.3;margin:.12rem 0}
.lm-wrap{text-align:center}
</style>
<div class="lm-wrap" id="rfWrap">
  <canvas id="rfCanvas" width="620" height="290" style="background:#fff;border:1px solid #ddd;border-radius:8px;max-width:100%"></canvas>
  <div class="lm-row">
    <button class="lm-btn on" data-mode="ok">well specified</button>
    <button class="lm-btn" data-mode="nonlin">non-linear</button>
    <button class="lm-btn" data-mode="hetero">heteroscedastic</button>
    &nbsp; noise <input id="rfNz" type="range" autocomplete="off" min="0.1" max="1" step="0.05" value="0.35" style="vertical-align:middle;width:90px"> <b id="rfNzv">0.35</b> &nbsp; <button class="lm-btn" id="rfNew">↻ resample</button>
  </div>
</div>
<script>
(function () {
  var cv = document.getElementById('rfCanvas'); if (!cv || cv.dataset.init) return; cv.dataset.init = 1;
  var c = cv.getContext('2d'), W = cv.width, H = cv.height, N = 60, mode = 'ok', Xr = [], Z = [];
  var nzEl = document.getElementById('rfNz');
  function gauss() { var u = 0, v = 0; while (!u) u = Math.random(); while (!v) v = Math.random(); return Math.sqrt(-2 * Math.log(u)) * Math.cos(2 * Math.PI * v); }
  function regen() { Xr = []; Z = []; for (var i = 0; i < N; i++) { Xr.push(-1.3 + 2.6 * Math.random()); Z.push(gauss()); } }
  function yOf(i) { var x = Xr[i], nz = +nzEl.value; if (mode === 'nonlin') return 0.3 + 0.6 * x + 0.9 * x * x + nz * Z[i]; if (mode === 'hetero') return 0.3 + 1.0 * x + nz * (0.3 + 1.4 * (x + 1.3) / 2.6) * Z[i] * 3; return 0.3 + 1.0 * x + nz * Z[i]; }
  function draw() {
    document.getElementById('rfNzv').textContent = (+nzEl.value).toFixed(2);
    var Y = [], i, mx = 0, my = 0; for (i = 0; i < N; i++) { Y.push(yOf(i)); mx += Xr[i]; my += Y[i]; } mx /= N; my /= N;
    var sxy = 0, sxx = 0; for (i = 0; i < N; i++) { sxy += (Xr[i] - mx) * (Y[i] - my); sxx += (Xr[i] - mx) * (Xr[i] - mx); }
    var b1 = sxy / sxx, b0 = my - b1 * mx, yh = [], res = []; for (i = 0; i < N; i++) { yh.push(b0 + b1 * Xr[i]); res.push(Y[i] - yh[i]); }
    var ymin = 1e9, ymax = -1e9, rmax = 1e-6, yhmin = 1e9, yhmax = -1e9; for (i = 0; i < N; i++) { ymin = Math.min(ymin, Y[i]); ymax = Math.max(ymax, Y[i]); rmax = Math.max(rmax, Math.abs(res[i])); yhmin = Math.min(yhmin, yh[i]); yhmax = Math.max(yhmax, yh[i]); }
    c.clearRect(0, 0, W, H); var gap = 24, pw = (W - gap) / 2, ph = H - 34, top = 8;
    // left: data + line
    var lx0 = 30, lx1 = pw - 6, xlo = -1.5, xhi = 1.5; function LX(x) { return lx0 + (x - xlo) / (xhi - xlo) * (lx1 - lx0); } function LY(y) { return top + (ymax + 0.2 - y) / ((ymax - ymin) + 0.4) * ph; }
    c.strokeStyle = '#ddd'; c.strokeRect(lx0, top, lx1 - lx0, ph); c.fillStyle = '#777'; c.font = '11px sans-serif'; c.textAlign = 'center'; c.fillText('data (x, Y) + linear fit', (lx0 + lx1) / 2, H - 6);
    c.strokeStyle = '#e74c3c'; c.lineWidth = 2; c.beginPath(); c.moveTo(LX(xlo), LY(b0 + b1 * xlo)); c.lineTo(LX(xhi), LY(b0 + b1 * xhi)); c.stroke();
    c.fillStyle = 'rgba(44,62,80,0.7)'; for (i = 0; i < N; i++) { c.beginPath(); c.arc(LX(Xr[i]), LY(Y[i]), 2.6, 0, 6.2832); c.fill(); }
    // right: residual vs fitted
    var rx0 = pw + gap, rx1 = W - 10; function RX(x) { return rx0 + (x - (yhmin - 0.2)) / ((yhmax - yhmin) + 0.4) * (rx1 - rx0); } function RY(r) { return top + (rmax * 1.15 - r) / (2.3 * rmax) * ph; }
    c.strokeStyle = '#ddd'; c.strokeRect(rx0, top, rx1 - rx0, ph); c.fillStyle = '#777'; c.fillText('residuals vs fitted', (rx0 + rx1) / 2, H - 6);
    c.strokeStyle = '#aaa'; c.setLineDash([4, 3]); c.beginPath(); c.moveTo(rx0, RY(0)); c.lineTo(rx1, RY(0)); c.stroke(); c.setLineDash([]);
    c.fillStyle = 'rgba(231,76,60,0.7)'; for (i = 0; i < N; i++) { c.beginPath(); c.arc(RX(yh[i]), RY(res[i]), 2.6, 0, 6.2832); c.fill(); }
  }
  function setMode(m) { mode = m; Array.prototype.forEach.call(document.querySelectorAll('#rfWrap .lm-btn[data-mode]'), function (b) { b.classList.toggle('on', b.dataset.mode === m); }); draw(); }
  Array.prototype.forEach.call(document.querySelectorAll('#rfWrap .lm-btn[data-mode]'), function (b) { b.addEventListener('click', function () { setMode(b.dataset.mode); }); });
  nzEl.addEventListener('input', draw);
  document.getElementById('rfNew').addEventListener('click', function () { regen(); draw(); });
  regen(); draw();
})();
</script>
```

## Homoscedasticity test (Breusch–Pagan) {.smaller}


. . .

We want to test whether $\Var(\varepsilon_i)=\sigma^2, ~~\forall i$

. . .

**Principle**: Assume $\varepsilon_i$ has variance [$\sigma_i^2 = \sigma^2 + z_i^T\gamma$]{style="background-color: lightblue;"} where:

- [$z_i$ is a $k$-vector]{style="background-color: orange;"} of variables that might explain [heteroscedasticity]{style="background-color: orange;"} ([known]{style="background-color: yellow;"})
- **Default in R**: $z_i = (X_i^{(1)}, \ldots, X_i^{(p)})$, so $k = p$
- $\gamma$ is an [unknown]{style="background-color: yellow;"} $k$-dimensional parameter

. . .


. . .

$H_0: \gamma = 0$ ([homosced.]{style="background-color: lightgreen;"}) VS $H_1: \gamma \neq 0$ ([heterosced.]{style="background-color: orange;"})

. . .

**R function**: `bptest` from `lmtest` library

## Consequences of Heteroscedasticity

. . .

**What happens**:

- OLS estimation of $\beta$ is no longer optimal but remains consistent
- Inference tools (tests, confidence intervals) become invalid because they rely on $\hat{\sigma}^2$ estimation


## Solutions for Heteroscedasticity


- **Transformation**: Transform $Y$ (e.g., log transformation) to stabilize variance
- **Modeling**: Model heteroscedasticity explicitly and account for it in estimation
- **GLS**: Use Generalized Least Squares (not detailed here)


## log Y closes the funnel {.smaller}

::: {style="font-size:86%"}
The [same data]{style="background-color: yellow;"} refit on three scales. Raw $Y$: the residuals **fan out** — the noise is multiplicative, so the spread grows with $\E(Y)$. On $\log Y$: a **band**, and [Breusch–Pagan stops rejecting]{style="background-color: lightgreen;"}.
:::

```{=html}
<style>
.lm-btn{font-family:inherit;font-size:.85em;padding:.4em 1.1em;margin:.12em .22em;border:1px solid #bbb;border-radius:8px;background:#f4f4f4;color:#333;cursor:pointer}
.lm-btn.on{background:#3b6fb6;color:#fff;border-color:#3b6fb6}
.lm-row{font-size:.72em;line-height:2.3;margin:.12rem 0}
.lm-wrap{text-align:center}
</style>
<div class="lm-wrap" id="vsWrap">
  <canvas id="vsCanvas" width="620" height="270" style="background:#fff;border:1px solid #ddd;border-radius:8px;max-width:100%"></canvas>
  <div class="lm-row">
    <button class="lm-btn on" data-mode="raw">Y</button>
    <button class="lm-btn" data-mode="sqrt">&radic;Y</button>
    <button class="lm-btn" data-mode="log">log Y</button>
    &nbsp; noise &sigma; <input id="vsNz" type="range" autocomplete="off" min="0.1" max="0.6" step="0.05" value="0.3" style="vertical-align:middle;width:90px"> <b id="vsNzv">0.30</b> &nbsp; <button class="lm-btn" id="vsNew">&#8635; resample</button>
  </div>
  <div class="lm-row">Breusch&ndash;Pagan \(\chi^2_1\) = <b id="vsBP">&ndash;</b> &nbsp; p = <b id="vsP">&ndash;</b> &nbsp;&middot;&nbsp; residual spread, top third / bottom third of \(\widehat Y\) = <b id="vsR">&ndash;</b></div>
</div>
<script>
(function () {
  var cv = document.getElementById('vsCanvas'); if (!cv || cv.dataset.init) return; cv.dataset.init = 1;
  var c = cv.getContext('2d'), W = cv.width, H = cv.height, N = 70, KEY = 'lmVarStab';
  var mode = 'raw', Xr = [], Z = [], nzEl = document.getElementById('vsNz');
  var LAB = { raw: 'Y', sqrt: '√Y', log: 'log Y' };
  function gauss() { var u = 0, v = 0; while (!u) u = Math.random(); while (!v) v = Math.random(); return Math.sqrt(-2 * Math.log(u)) * Math.cos(2 * Math.PI * v); }
  // erfc via Abramowitz & Stegun 7.1.26 (|err| < 1.5e-7), kept in the e^{-x^2} form so
  // the upper tail stays accurate: P(chi2_1 > t) = erfc(sqrt(t/2)).
  function erfc(x) { var t = 1 / (1 + 0.3275911 * x); return t * (0.254829592 + t * (-0.284496736 + t * (1.421413741 + t * (-1.453152027 + t * 1.061405429)))) * Math.exp(-x * x); }
  function regen() { Xr = []; Z = []; for (var i = 0; i < N; i++) { Xr.push(0.2 + 1.8 * Math.random()); Z.push(gauss()); } }
  // Y = exp(b0 + b1 x + sigma Z): homoscedastic on the LOG scale, so on the raw scale
  // sd(Y|x) is proportional to E(Y|x) — the textbook multiplicative-error situation.
  function g(y) { return mode === 'log' ? Math.log(y) : mode === 'sqrt' ? Math.sqrt(y) : y; }
  function draw() {
    var i, sg = +nzEl.value;
    document.getElementById('vsNzv').textContent = sg.toFixed(2);
    var V = [], mx = 0, my = 0;
    for (i = 0; i < N; i++) { V.push(g(Math.exp(0.5 + 1.1 * Xr[i] + sg * Z[i]))); mx += Xr[i]; my += V[i]; }
    mx /= N; my /= N;
    var sxy = 0, sxx = 0;
    for (i = 0; i < N; i++) { sxy += (Xr[i] - mx) * (V[i] - my); sxx += (Xr[i] - mx) * (Xr[i] - mx); }
    var b1 = sxy / sxx, b0 = my - b1 * mx, yh = [], res = [];
    for (i = 0; i < N; i++) { yh.push(b0 + b1 * Xr[i]); res.push(V[i] - yh[i]); }
    // Breusch-Pagan, Koenker's studentized form (R's bptest default): n * R^2 of the
    // auxiliary regression of the squared residuals on x.
    var e2 = [], m2 = 0;
    for (i = 0; i < N; i++) { e2.push(res[i] * res[i]); m2 += res[i] * res[i]; }
    m2 /= N;
    var sxe = 0, see = 0;
    for (i = 0; i < N; i++) { sxe += (Xr[i] - mx) * (e2[i] - m2); see += (e2[i] - m2) * (e2[i] - m2); }
    var bp = see > 0 ? N * (sxe * sxe / sxx) / see : 0, pv = erfc(Math.sqrt(bp / 2));
    // residual spread in the top vs the bottom third of the fitted values
    var ord = []; for (i = 0; i < N; i++) ord.push(i);
    ord.sort(function (a, b) { return yh[a] - yh[b]; });
    var t3 = Math.floor(N / 3);
    function sd(ix) { var m = 0, s = 0, k; for (k = 0; k < ix.length; k++) m += res[ix[k]]; m /= ix.length; for (k = 0; k < ix.length; k++) s += (res[ix[k]] - m) * (res[ix[k]] - m); return Math.sqrt(s / (ix.length - 1)); }
    var ratio = sd(ord.slice(N - t3)) / sd(ord.slice(0, t3));
    var vmin = 1e9, vmax = -1e9, rmax = 1e-9, hmin = 1e9, hmax = -1e9;
    for (i = 0; i < N; i++) {
      if (V[i] < vmin) vmin = V[i]; if (V[i] > vmax) vmax = V[i];
      if (Math.abs(res[i]) > rmax) rmax = Math.abs(res[i]);
      if (yh[i] < hmin) hmin = yh[i]; if (yh[i] > hmax) hmax = yh[i];
    }
    c.clearRect(0, 0, W, H);
    c.font = '11px sans-serif'; c.lineWidth = 1;
    var gap = 26, pw = (W - gap) / 2, ph = H - 34, top = 8;
    // ---- left: the data on the chosen scale, with its least-squares line
    var lx0 = 30, lx1 = pw - 6, xlo = 0, xhi = 2.2;
    function LX(x) { return lx0 + (x - xlo) / (xhi - xlo) * (lx1 - lx0); }
    function LY(y) { return top + (vmax + (vmax - vmin) * 0.08 - y) / ((vmax - vmin) * 1.16) * ph; }
    c.strokeStyle = '#e6e6e6'; c.strokeRect(lx0, top, lx1 - lx0, ph);
    c.fillStyle = '#777'; c.textAlign = 'center'; c.fillText('data (x, ' + LAB[mode] + ') + fit', (lx0 + lx1) / 2, H - 6);
    c.save(); c.beginPath(); c.rect(lx0, top, lx1 - lx0, ph); c.clip();
    c.strokeStyle = '#e74c3c'; c.lineWidth = 2; c.beginPath();
    c.moveTo(LX(xlo), LY(b0 + b1 * xlo)); c.lineTo(LX(xhi), LY(b0 + b1 * xhi)); c.stroke();
    c.fillStyle = 'rgba(44,62,80,0.7)';
    for (i = 0; i < N; i++) { c.beginPath(); c.arc(LX(Xr[i]), LY(V[i]), 2.6, 0, 6.2832); c.fill(); }
    c.restore();
    c.textAlign = 'left'; c.fillStyle = '#8a9099'; c.fillText(LAB[mode], lx0 + 4, top + 12);
    // ---- right: residuals vs fitted, with the local spread as a +/-2 sd envelope
    var rx0 = pw + gap, rx1 = W - 10, pad = (hmax - hmin) * 0.08 + 1e-9;
    function RX(h) { return rx0 + (h - hmin + pad) / ((hmax - hmin) + 2 * pad) * (rx1 - rx0); }
    function RY(r) { return top + (rmax * 1.15 - r) / (2.3 * rmax) * ph; }
    c.strokeStyle = '#e6e6e6'; c.strokeRect(rx0, top, rx1 - rx0, ph);
    c.fillStyle = '#777'; c.textAlign = 'center'; c.fillText('residuals vs fitted', (rx0 + rx1) / 2, H - 6);
    var NB = 5, bx = [], bs = [];
    for (var j = 0; j < NB; j++) {
      var a = hmin + (hmax - hmin) * j / NB, b = hmin + (hmax - hmin) * (j + 1) / NB, ss = 0, cnt = 0;
      for (i = 0; i < N; i++) if (yh[i] >= a && (yh[i] < b || j === NB - 1)) { ss += res[i] * res[i]; cnt++; }
      if (cnt > 1) { bx.push((a + b) / 2); bs.push(Math.sqrt(ss / cnt)); }
    }
    // (1,2,1)-smooth the bin spreads, so the envelope shows the trend and not the
    // sampling noise of a dozen points per bin, and span the whole panel
    if (bs.length > 2) { var sm = bs.slice(); for (i = 1; i < bs.length - 1; i++) sm[i] = (bs[i - 1] + 2 * bs[i] + bs[i + 1]) / 4; bs = sm; }
    if (bx.length > 1) { bx[0] = hmin - pad; bx[bx.length - 1] = hmax + pad; }
    c.save(); c.beginPath(); c.rect(rx0, top, rx1 - rx0, ph); c.clip();
    if (bs.length > 1) {
      c.fillStyle = 'rgba(52,152,219,0.18)'; c.beginPath();
      for (i = 0; i < bx.length; i++) { var px = RX(bx[i]), py = RY(2 * bs[i]); i ? c.lineTo(px, py) : c.moveTo(px, py); }
      for (i = bx.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) c.lineTo(RX(bx[i]), RY(-2 * bs[i]));
      c.closePath(); c.fill();
    }
    c.strokeStyle = '#aaa'; c.setLineDash([4, 3]); c.beginPath(); c.moveTo(rx0, RY(0)); c.lineTo(rx1, RY(0)); c.stroke(); c.setLineDash([]);
    c.fillStyle = 'rgba(231,76,60,0.7)';
    for (i = 0; i < N; i++) { c.beginPath(); c.arc(RX(yh[i]), RY(res[i]), 2.6, 0, 6.2832); c.fill(); }
    c.restore();
    c.textAlign = 'left'; c.fillStyle = '#8a9099'; c.fillText('±2 sd, locally', rx0 + 4, top + 12);
    // ---- readouts
    document.getElementById('vsBP').textContent = bp.toFixed(2);
    var pEl = document.getElementById('vsP');
    pEl.textContent = pv < 0.001 ? '< 0.001' : pv.toFixed(3);
    pEl.style.color = pv < 0.05 ? '#c0392b' : '#27ae60';
    document.getElementById('vsR').textContent = ratio.toFixed(2) + '×';
  }
  function save() { try { localStorage.setItem(KEY, JSON.stringify({ m: mode, s: +nzEl.value })); } catch (e) {} }
  function setMode(m) {
    mode = m;
    Array.prototype.forEach.call(document.querySelectorAll('#vsWrap .lm-btn[data-mode]'), function (b) { b.classList.toggle('on', b.dataset.mode === m); });
    draw(); save();
  }
  Array.prototype.forEach.call(document.querySelectorAll('#vsWrap .lm-btn[data-mode]'), function (b) {
    b.addEventListener('click', function () { setMode(b.dataset.mode); });
  });
  nzEl.addEventListener('input', function () { draw(); save(); });
  document.getElementById('vsNew').addEventListener('click', function () { regen(); draw(); });
  var st = null; try { st = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(KEY)); } catch (e) {}
  if (st && st.s != null) nzEl.value = st.s;
  regen(); setMode(st && LAB[st.m] ? st.m : 'raw');
})();
</script>
```


## Non-correlation of errors

. . .

**Purpose**: Test if $\Var(\varepsilon)$ is diagonal (uncorrelated errors)

. . .

Correlation between $\varepsilon_i$ [often occurs with temporal data]{style="background-color: yellow;"} (index $i$ represents time)

. . .

**Auto-correlation Model of order $r$**:

::: {.square-def}
$$\varepsilon_i = \rho_1 \varepsilon_{i-1} + \dots + \rho_r \varepsilon_{i-r} + \eta_i$$
where $\eta_i \sim \text{iid } N(0, \sigma^2)$
:::



## Tests for Correlation {.smaller}

. . .

In the auto-correlation model [$\varepsilon_i = \rho_1 \varepsilon_{i-1} + \dots + \rho_r \varepsilon_{i-r} + \eta_i$]{style="background-color: lightblue;"}: 

. . .

**Durbin-Watson Test** (for $r = 1$ only):

- [$H_0: \rho_1 = 0$ VS $H_1: \rho_1 \neq 0$]{style="background-color: lightblue;"}
- **R function**: `dwtest` from `lmtest`

. . .

**Breusch-Godfrey Test** (for any $r$):

- [$H_0: \rho_1 = \cdots = \rho_r = 0$ VS $H_1:$ at least one $\rho_j \neq 0$]{style="background-color: lightblue;"}
- User chooses order $r$ (default $r = 1$)
- **R function**: `bgtest` from `lmtest`


## Consequences of Auto-correlation {.smaller}

- OLS estimation of $\beta$ is no longer optimal but remains consistent
- Inference tools (tests, confidence intervals) become invalid

. . .

**Solutions:**

- **GLS modeling**: Model the dependence structure (complex, risky if wrong)
- **Model improvement**: [Exploit the dependence]{style="background-color: yellow;"} to enhance the model
- **Ex**: [Explain $Y_i$ using $Y_{i-1}$]{style="background-color: yellow;"} in addition to $(X_i^{(1)}, \dots, X_i^{(p)})$

## Normality of residuals

. . .

**Purpose**: Examine normality of residuals $\hat \varepsilon$

**Reminder on Normality Assumption**

- **Not essential** when $n$ is large
- All tests remain **asymptotically valid**
- Only **prediction intervals** truly require normality

. . .


**Perhaps the least important assumption, but we can still examine it since**

If $\varepsilon \sim N(0, \sigma^2 I_n)$ then [$\hat{\varepsilon} \sim N(0, \sigma^2 P_{[X]}^{\perp})$]{style="background-color: lightblue;"}


## Diagnostic Tools for Normality of ε̂

. . .

**Q-Q Plot (Henry's line)**:

- Plot theoretical vs. sample quantiles of $\hat{\varepsilon}$
- **R function**: `qqnorm`

. . .

**Shapiro-Wilk, $\chi^2$ or KS Tests**:

- Formal test of normality for $\hat{\varepsilon}$
- $H_0$: residuals are normally distributed
- $H_1$: residuals are not normally distributed
- **R function**: `shapiro.test`


## Q–Q plot of the residuals {.smaller}

. . .


::: {style="font-size:86%"}
Sorted standardized residuals vs theoretical normal quantiles. **On the line** ⇒ normal; an **S-shape** ⇒ skew, **steep tails** ⇒ heavy tails. Pick the error distribution.
:::

```{=html}
<style>
.lm-btn{font-family:inherit;font-size:.85em;padding:.4em 1.1em;margin:.12em .22em;border:1px solid #bbb;border-radius:8px;background:#f4f4f4;color:#333;cursor:pointer}
.lm-btn.on{background:#3b6fb6;color:#fff;border-color:#3b6fb6}
.lm-row{font-size:.72em;line-height:2.3;margin:.12rem 0}
.lm-wrap{text-align:center}
</style>
<div class="lm-wrap" id="qqWrap">
  <canvas id="qqCanvas" width="360" height="320" style="background:#fff;border:1px solid #ddd;border-radius:8px;max-width:100%"></canvas>
  <div class="lm-row">
    <button class="lm-btn on" data-mode="normal">normal</button>
    <button class="lm-btn" data-mode="skew">right-skewed</button>
    <button class="lm-btn" data-mode="heavy">heavy-tailed</button>
    &nbsp; N <input id="qqN" type="range" autocomplete="off" min="15" max="200" step="1" value="60" style="vertical-align:middle;width:100px"> <b id="qqNv">60</b> &nbsp; <button class="lm-btn" id="qqNew">↻ resample</button>
  </div>
</div>
<script>
(function () {
  var cv = document.getElementById('qqCanvas'); if (!cv || cv.dataset.init) return; cv.dataset.init = 1;
  var c = cv.getContext('2d'), W = cv.width, H = cv.height, MAXN = 200, mode = 'normal', U = [];
  var nEl = document.getElementById('qqN');
  function gauss() { var u = 0, v = 0; while (!u) u = Math.random(); while (!v) v = Math.random(); return Math.sqrt(-2 * Math.log(u)) * Math.cos(2 * Math.PI * v); }
  function qnorm(p) { var a = [-3.969683028665376e1, 2.209460984245205e2, -2.759285104469687e2, 1.38357751867269e2, -3.066479806614716e1, 2.506628277459239], b = [-5.447609879822406e1, 1.615858368580409e2, -1.556989798598866e2, 6.680131188771972e1, -1.328068155288572e1], cc = [-7.784894002430293e-3, -3.223964580411365e-1, -2.400758277161838, -2.549732539343734, 4.374664141464968, 2.938163982698783], d = [7.784695709041462e-3, 3.224671290700398e-1, 2.445134137142996, 3.754408661907416], pl = 0.02425, q, r; if (p < pl) { q = Math.sqrt(-2 * Math.log(p)); return (((((cc[0] * q + cc[1]) * q + cc[2]) * q + cc[3]) * q + cc[4]) * q + cc[5]) / ((((d[0] * q + d[1]) * q + d[2]) * q + d[3]) * q + 1); } if (p <= 1 - pl) { q = p - 0.5; r = q * q; return (((((a[0] * r + a[1]) * r + a[2]) * r + a[3]) * r + a[4]) * r + a[5]) * q / (((((b[0] * r + b[1]) * r + b[2]) * r + b[3]) * r + b[4]) * r + 1); } q = Math.sqrt(-2 * Math.log(1 - p)); return -(((((cc[0] * q + cc[1]) * q + cc[2]) * q + cc[3]) * q + cc[4]) * q + cc[5]) / ((((d[0] * q + d[1]) * q + d[2]) * q + d[3]) * q + 1); }
  function regen() { U = []; for (var i = 0; i < MAXN; i++) U.push([Math.random(), Math.random(), gauss(), gauss(), gauss(), gauss()]); }   // stored randoms per index (nested in N)
  function sample(i) { var u = U[i]; if (mode === 'skew') return -Math.log(u[0]); if (mode === 'heavy') return u[2] / Math.sqrt((u[3] * u[3] + u[4] * u[4] + u[5] * u[5]) / 3); return u[2]; }   // skew=exp, heavy=t(3)
  function draw() {
    var n = +nEl.value, i; document.getElementById('qqNv').textContent = n;
    var s = []; for (i = 0; i < n; i++) s.push(sample(i)); var m = 0; s.forEach(function (v) { m += v; }); m /= n; var sd = 0; s.forEach(function (v) { sd += (v - m) * (v - m); }); sd = Math.sqrt(sd / (n - 1)) || 1;
    s = s.map(function (v) { return (v - m) / sd; }).sort(function (a, b) { return a - b; });
    var R = 3.4, pad = 30; function PX(x) { return pad + (x + R) / (2 * R) * (W - pad - 10); } function PY(y) { return H - pad - (y + R) / (2 * R) * (H - pad - 10); }
    c.clearRect(0, 0, W, H); c.strokeStyle = '#ddd'; c.strokeRect(pad, 10, W - pad - 10, H - pad - 10);
    c.strokeStyle = '#aaa'; c.setLineDash([5, 4]); c.beginPath(); c.moveTo(PX(-R), PY(-R)); c.lineTo(PX(R), PY(R)); c.stroke(); c.setLineDash([]);
    c.fillStyle = 'rgba(44,62,80,0.75)'; for (i = 0; i < n; i++) { var th = qnorm((i + 0.5) / n); c.beginPath(); c.arc(PX(Math.max(-R, Math.min(R, th))), PY(Math.max(-R, Math.min(R, s[i]))), 2.6, 0, 6.2832); c.fill(); }
    c.fillStyle = '#777'; c.font = '11px sans-serif'; c.textAlign = 'center'; c.fillText('theoretical N(0,1) quantiles', W / 2 + 8, H - 6);
    c.save(); c.translate(12, H / 2); c.rotate(-Math.PI / 2); c.fillText('sample quantiles', 0, 0); c.restore();
  }
  function setMode(m) { mode = m; Array.prototype.forEach.call(document.querySelectorAll('#qqWrap .lm-btn[data-mode]'), function (b) { b.classList.toggle('on', b.dataset.mode === m); }); draw(); }
  Array.prototype.forEach.call(document.querySelectorAll('#qqWrap .lm-btn[data-mode]'), function (b) { b.addEventListener('click', function () { setMode(b.dataset.mode); }); });
  nEl.addEventListener('input', draw);
  document.getElementById('qqNew').addEventListener('click', function () { regen(); draw(); });
  regen(); draw();
})();
</script>
```

# Outliers and Influential Points

## Outlier Analysis

. . .

An individual is atypical when:

1. **Poorly explained** by the model, and/or
2. **Heavily influences** coefficient estimation

. . .

**Identify** these individuals to:

- **Understand** the reason for this particularity
- **Potentially modify** the model accordingly  
- **Potentially exclude** the individual from the study


## Poorly explained: standardized residuals {.smaller}

. . .

Individual $i$ is poorly explained if its residual [$\hat{\varepsilon}_i$ is "abnormally" large]{style="background-color: yellow;"}.

. . .

**How to quantify "abnormally"?**

Let [$h_{ij}$]{style="background-color: lightblue;"} be elements of matrix $P_{[X]}$ (hat matrix).

For a Gaussian model: [$\hat{\varepsilon}_i \sim N(0, (1-h_{ii})\sigma^2)$]{style="background-color: lightblue;"}


. . .

**Standardized Residuals**

::: {.square-def}
$$t_i = \frac{\hat{\varepsilon}_i}{\hat{\sigma}\sqrt{1-h_{ii}}}$$
:::


## Poorly explained: the test

. . .

::: {.square-def}
$$h_{ij} = (P_{[X]})_{ij} \and t_i = \frac{\hat{\varepsilon}_i}{\hat{\sigma}\sqrt{1-h_{ii}}}$$

:::



. . .

We expect $t_i \sim St(n-p)$ (not strictly true since $\hat{\varepsilon}_i \not\perp \hat{\sigma}^2$)

::: {.callout-note}
## Definition
Individual $i$ is considered poorly explained by the model if:
$$|t_i| > t_{n-p}(1-\alpha/2)$$
for predetermined $\alpha$, typically $\alpha = 0.05$, giving $t_{n-p}(1-\alpha/2) \approx 2$.
:::



## Leverage Points

. . .

A point is influential if it [contributes significantly to $\hat{\beta}$]{style="background-color: yellow;"} estimation.

. . .

**Leverage value**: $h_{ii}$ corresponds to the weight of $Y_i$ on its own estimation $\hat{Y}_i$

. . .

We know that: $\sum_{i=1}^n h_{ii} = \text{tr}(P_{[X]}) = p$

. . .

Therefore, on average: $h_{ii} \approx p/n$

. . .

::: {.callout-note}
## Definition
Individual $i$ is called a **leverage point** if $h_{ii} \gg p/n$

Typically: $h_{ii} > 2p/n$ or $h_{ii} > 3p/n$
:::


## Outlier Analysis: Cook's Distance

. . .

**Cook's Distance**

Quantifies the influence of individual $i$ on $\hat{Y}$:

::: {.square-def}
$$C_i = \frac{\|\hat{Y} - \hat{Y}_{(-i)}\|^2}{p\hat{\sigma}^2}$$
:::


where $\hat{Y}_{(-i)} = X\hat{\beta}_{(-i)}$ with $\hat{\beta}_{(-i)}$: estimation of $\beta$ without individual $i$


## Cook's Distance, Alternative Formula

. . .

::: {.square-def}
$$C_i = \frac{1}{p} \cdot \frac{h_{ii}}{1-h_{ii}} \cdot t_i^2,$$
:::


where [$t_i = \frac{\hat{\varepsilon}_i}{\hat{\sigma}\sqrt{1-h_{ii}}}$]{style="background-color: lightblue;"}.

This formula shows that Cook's distance $C_i$ combines:

1. **Aberrant effect** of individual (through $t_i$)
2. **Leverage effect** (through $h_{ii}$)

. . .

**R functions**: `cooks.distance` and last plot of `plot.lm`


## Outlier, leverage, influence {.smaller}

. . .


::: {style="font-size:84%"}
**Drag the gold point.** OLS line (solid) vs the fit *without* it (dashed). **Outlier** = large residual $|t_i|>2$ (aberrant in $Y$). **Leverage** = extreme in $x$, $h_{ii}>2p/n$. **Influential** = it moves the fit: Cook's $C_i=\frac1p\frac{h_{ii}}{1-h_{ii}}t_i^2>4/n$ — a mixture of the two.
:::

```{=html}
<style>
.lm-btn{font-family:inherit;font-size:.85em;padding:.4em 1.1em;margin:.12em .22em;border:1px solid #bbb;border-radius:8px;background:#f4f4f4;color:#333;cursor:pointer}
.lm-row{font-size:.72em;line-height:2.3;margin:.1rem 0}
.lm-wrap{text-align:center}
</style>
<div class="lm-wrap">
  <canvas id="ckCanvas" width="560" height="300" style="background:#fff;border:1px solid #ddd;border-radius:8px;max-width:100%;touch-action:none;cursor:grab"></canvas>
  <div class="lm-row">\(h_{ii}\)=<b id="ckH">–</b> (leverage if &gt; 2p/n=<b id="ckHt">–</b>) &nbsp;·&nbsp; \(|t_i|\)=<b id="ckT">–</b> (outlier if &gt; 2) &nbsp;·&nbsp; \(C_i\)=<b id="ckC">–</b> (infl. if &gt; 4/n=<b id="ckCt">–</b>)</div>
  <div class="lm-row">status: <b id="ckMsg">–</b> &nbsp; <button class="lm-btn" id="ckNew">↻ new data</button></div>
</div>
<script>
(function () {
  var cv = document.getElementById('ckCanvas'); if (!cv || cv.dataset.init) return; cv.dataset.init = 1;
  var c = cv.getContext('2d'), W = cv.width, H = cv.height, N = 16, p = 2, P = [], drag = -1;
  var XL = -3.4, XH = 3.4, YL = -3.4, YH = 3.4;
  function gauss() { var u = 0, v = 0; while (!u) u = Math.random(); while (!v) v = Math.random(); return Math.sqrt(-2 * Math.log(u)) * Math.cos(2 * Math.PI * v); }
  function regen() { P = []; for (var i = 0; i < N - 1; i++) { var x = gauss() * 1.2; P.push([x, 0.8 * x + gauss() * 0.5]); } P.push([2.4, 0.3]); }
  function PX(x) { return 30 + (x - XL) / (XH - XL) * (W - 44); } function PY(y) { return H - 22 - (y - YL) / (YH - YL) * (H - 36); }
  function IX(px) { return XL + (px - 30) / (W - 44) * (XH - XL); } function IY(py) { return YL + (H - 22 - py) / (H - 36) * (YH - YL); }
  function pos(e) { var r = cv.getBoundingClientRect(); return [(e.clientX - r.left) * W / r.width, (e.clientY - r.top) * H / r.height]; }
  function ols(pts) { var n = pts.length, mx = 0, my = 0; pts.forEach(function (q) { mx += q[0]; my += q[1]; }); mx /= n; my /= n; var sxy = 0, sxx = 0; pts.forEach(function (q) { sxy += (q[0] - mx) * (q[1] - my); sxx += (q[0] - mx) * (q[0] - mx); }); var b1 = sxy / (sxx || 1e-9); return [my - b1 * mx, b1, mx, sxx]; }
  function draw() {
    var f = ols(P), b0 = f[0], b1 = f[1], xbar = f[2], Sxx = f[3], i, n = N;
    var ssr = 0; for (i = 0; i < n; i++) { var e = P[i][1] - (b0 + b1 * P[i][0]); ssr += e * e; } var sig = Math.sqrt(ssr / (n - p));
    var sp = P[n - 1], hii = 1 / n + (sp[0] - xbar) * (sp[0] - xbar) / (Sxx || 1e-9), resi = sp[1] - (b0 + b1 * sp[0]);
    var ti = resi / (sig * Math.sqrt(Math.max(1e-6, 1 - hii))), Ci = (1 / p) * (hii / Math.max(1e-6, 1 - hii)) * ti * ti;
    var hThr = 2 * p / n, cThr = 4 / n, isLev = hii > hThr, isOut = Math.abs(ti) > 2, isInfl = Ci > cThr;
    var f2 = ols(P.slice(0, n - 1));
    c.clearRect(0, 0, W, H);
    c.strokeStyle = '#eee'; c.lineWidth = 1; c.beginPath(); c.moveTo(PX(XL), PY(0)); c.lineTo(PX(XH), PY(0)); c.moveTo(PX(0), PY(YL)); c.lineTo(PX(0), PY(YH)); c.stroke();
    c.strokeStyle = '#999'; c.setLineDash([5, 4]); c.lineWidth = 1.5; c.beginPath(); c.moveTo(PX(XL), PY(f2[0] + f2[1] * XL)); c.lineTo(PX(XH), PY(f2[0] + f2[1] * XH)); c.stroke(); c.setLineDash([]);
    c.strokeStyle = '#e74c3c'; c.lineWidth = 2.5; c.beginPath(); c.moveTo(PX(XL), PY(b0 + b1 * XL)); c.lineTo(PX(XH), PY(b0 + b1 * XH)); c.stroke();
    c.fillStyle = 'rgba(44,62,80,0.75)'; for (i = 0; i < n - 1; i++) { c.beginPath(); c.arc(PX(P[i][0]), PY(P[i][1]), 3.4, 0, 6.2832); c.fill(); }
    var col = isInfl ? '#e74c3c' : (isLev ? '#3b6fb6' : (isOut ? '#e67e22' : '#ffd23f'));
    c.fillStyle = col; c.strokeStyle = '#000'; c.lineWidth = 1.5; c.beginPath(); c.arc(PX(sp[0]), PY(sp[1]), 7, 0, 6.2832); c.fill(); c.stroke();
    document.getElementById('ckH').textContent = hii.toFixed(3); document.getElementById('ckHt').textContent = hThr.toFixed(3);
    document.getElementById('ckT').textContent = Math.abs(ti).toFixed(2); document.getElementById('ckC').textContent = Ci.toFixed(3); document.getElementById('ckCt').textContent = cThr.toFixed(3);
    var tags = []; if (isLev) tags.push('<span style="color:#3b6fb6">leverage</span>'); if (isOut) tags.push('<span style="color:#e67e22">outlier</span>'); if (isInfl) tags.push('<span style="color:#e74c3c"><b>influential</b></span>');
    document.getElementById('ckMsg').innerHTML = tags.length ? tags.join(' · ') : '<span style="color:#1b7a3a">typical point</span>';
  }
  cv.addEventListener('pointerdown', function (e) { var q = pos(e); if (Math.hypot(PX(P[N - 1][0]) - q[0], PY(P[N - 1][1]) - q[1]) < 16) { drag = N - 1; cv.style.cursor = 'grabbing'; } });
  window.addEventListener('pointermove', function (e) { if (drag < 0) return; var q = pos(e); P[drag] = [Math.max(XL, Math.min(XH, IX(q[0]))), Math.max(YL, Math.min(YH, IY(q[1])))]; draw(); e.preventDefault(); });
  window.addEventListener('pointerup', function () { drag = -1; cv.style.cursor = 'grab'; });
  document.getElementById('ckNew').addEventListener('click', function () { regen(); draw(); });
  regen(); draw();
})();
</script>
```
